units.source_text: 继而又说：“已故的母后藤壶道人，书法功夫甚深，具有秀丽之趣。

en.t: He went on to say, "The late Empress Mother Fujitsubo, who had taken religious vows, had deeply cultivated calligraphy and possessed an elegant charm.

units.source_text: 然而笔力较弱，未免缺乏余韵。

en.t: Yet her brushwork was somewhat weak, and inevitably lacked lingering resonance.

units.source_text: 尚侍胧月夜确是当代名家，但是过于潇洒，亦是美中不足。

en.t: The Naishi no Kami Oborozukiyo is certainly a master of our age, but she is too free and elegant, which is also a flaw in her beauty.

units.source_text: 虽然如此，总之，尚侍胧月夜、前斋院槿姬与你，都是书法名手。”

en.t: Even so, in short, Oborozukiyo, the former Kamo Priestess Princess Asagao, and you are all masters of calligraphy."

units.source_text: 他称赞紫姬的书法。

en.t: He praised Lady Murasaki's calligraphy.

units.source_text: 紫姬答道：“把我列入名手，教人惭愧死了！”

en.t: Lady Murasaki replied, "To count me among such masters makes me feel terribly ashamed!"

units.source_text: 源氏说：“你也不须过分谦逊。

en.t: Genji said, "You need not be so excessively modest.

units.source_text: 你的笔法柔丽可爱，自有特色。

en.t: Your brush style is soft, graceful, and charming, with a character all its own.

units.source_text: 不过你的汉字太高明了，假名赶不上它，不免略有破笔。”

en.t: Only, your Chinese characters are so superb that your kana cannot quite match them, and the brushwork becomes a little uneven."

units.source_text: 他又添置几本没有写过字的空白册子，封面与带子都很精美。

en.t: He also obtained several blank booklets that had not yet been written in, with very beautiful covers and ties.

units.source_text: 他说：“我想请萤兵部卿亲王和左卫门督也写一点。

en.t: He said, "I would like to ask Prince Hotaru, the Minister of War, and the Captain of the Left Gate Guards to write something as well.

units.source_text: 我自己拟写两册。

en.t: I intend to write two booklets myself.

units.source_text: 他们无论怎样高明，总比不上我吧。”

en.t: No matter how skilled they may be, surely they cannot surpass me."

units.source_text: 这是自夸了。

en.t: This was boasting.

units.source_text: 他又精选笔墨，郑重其事地写信与诸位夫人，请她们也写册子。

en.t: He also carefully selected brushes and ink, and solemnly wrote letters to the ladies, asking them to write booklets too.

units.source_text: 诸位夫人都以为此事甚难。

en.t: All the ladies thought this was a very difficult matter.

units.source_text: 就中有推却者，源氏再度诚恳请托。

en.t: When some among them declined, Genji earnestly asked them again.

units.source_text: 他又选取几本非常华丽的、染成颜色上深下渐淡的高丽纸册子，要叫几个风流少年也都试书。

en.t: He then selected several very splendid booklets of Korean paper, dyed darker at the top and gradually paler below, intending to have several elegant young men try writing in them too.

units.source_text: 对宰相中将夕雾、式部卿亲王的儿子左兵卫督、及内大臣家头中将柏木说道：“苇手、歌绘都好，各用自己所心爱的字体可也。”

en.t: To Yugiri, the Consultant Captain, to the Captain of the Left Guards, son of the Prince Minister of Ceremonial, and to Kashiwagi, the Chamberlain Lieutenant from the Minister of the Center's household, he said, "Reed-hand or poem-pictures are both fine; each of you may use whatever style you like best."

units.source_text: 于是诸少年各自用心书写，互相竞争。

en.t: Thus the young men each wrote with care, competing with one another.
